content.title: About
content.content: Yellow onions are mature onion bulbs harvested when the skin turns fully yellow. They have a characteristic sweet flavor and aroma that intensifies with cooking. Raw yellow onions are commonly used in salads, salsas, and as a garnish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Yellow onions store longer than green onions because of their lower moisture content.
They contain sulfur compounds that release volatile gases when cut, causing tears.
In many cultures yellow onions symbolize purity and are used in rituals.
Among onion varieties, yellow has the highest sugar content, making it less pungent.
Onions were first domesticated in Central Asia over 5,000 years ago.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Contains quercetin and sulfides that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Flavonoids help lower cholesterol levels and improve vessel function.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immunity and participates in collagen synthesis.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to onions.

items.title: Stomach irritation
items.content: Raw onions can cause discomfort in people with sensitive stomachs.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Sulfur compounds may lead to increased gas production and bloating.

items.title: Interaction with medications
items.content: Large amounts of onion can enhance the effects of anticoagulants.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice raw yellow onions thinly or dice them and add to salads, sandwiches, guacamole, and marinades. They can also be pickled in vinegar or lemon juice to mellow the flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store onions in a cool, dry, dark place with good ventilation. Properly stored, they stay fresh for several weeks. Keep them away from potatoes, as they accelerate each other's spoilage.
